issues.title: Ranked-run integrity: difficulty lock enforced at consumption + Alpha Tools sticky unranked flag (#1084)
issues.body:
Closes #1084. Implements the Alpha Tools ruling (decision card
docs/decision-cards/2026-08-01_dev-powers-nomenclature.html, ruled via PR #1096).
Related: #1058 (the lock this fixes the enforcement of), #1060 (the pattern copied).

Two pieces, one PR, because they share a mechanism: GameConfig.is_ranked_run() / the
GameConfig choke point.

## Piece 1 -- #1084: enforce the difficulty lock at CONSUMPTION

**Option chosen: a hybrid of the issue's options 1 and 2** -- a named accessor
GameConfig.effective_difficulty() (option 2's shape), consumed by
GameManager._apply_difficulty_settings() (option 1's location). Why:

- Option 1 alone repeats the #1058 mistake one level down: the rule would live inside
  one function body with nothing naming it, so the NEXT consumer of difficulty reads
  the raw field again. The accessor is the #1060 lesson: a named choke point a future
  caller cannot forget.
- Option 3 (route non-Standard through is_ranked_run) was rejected for now: while the
  Settings dropdown is disabled there is no legitimate way to HOLD a non-Standard
  difficulty, so option 3 would only ever fire on a stale config.cfg -- punishing a
  player with an unranked run for a value they cannot even see or change. Revisit when
  the lock lifts.
- Website #191 froze the submission surface; 1/2 change nothing that is submitted.

Mechanics:
- The raw difficulty field is now the stored PREFERENCE (untouched, persists,
  honoured the day LEAGUE_DIFFICULTY_LOCK flips false); effective_difficulty() is what
  runs PLAY at. pregame_setup no longer stomps the raw field.
- Settings + pregame dropdowns: disabled with the ONE shared tooltip
  (GameConfig.DIFFICULTY_LOCK_TOOLTIP), and their change-handlers refuse to write
  while locked (belt-and-braces; the guarantee is at consumption).
- Kept the #447 invalid-value healing; invalid persisted values degrade to Standard
  even when unlocked.
- **Settings-layout lane note:** feat/settings-operations-board owns the difficulty
  ROW's layout; this PR touches only selected/disabled/tooltip + the write guard in
  _on_difficulty_changed. Expect a small merge there.

## Piece 2 -- Alpha Tools (exclude and tell them, three times)

- GameConfig.alpha_tools_used: **sticky, one-way, RUN-scoped**. Set by
  mark_alpha_tools_used(turn) at the moment of actual state mutation; toggling the
  tool off does not clear it; ONLY start_new_game resets it; the SaveLoad envelope
  carries it (additive optional keys, old saves load clean) so a save/load cycle can
  neither launder a tainted run nor smear taint onto a clean save.
- is_ranked_run() now gates on scenario_id OR alpha_tools_used -- the single
  board-write site (GameOverScreen._persist_and_submit_score) needed no change.
- Warnings, settled wording from the card, established NOT RANKED amber
  Color(1.0, 0.75, 0.25), shown never silent (#1027):
  1. on both toggle surfaces ("[!] ALPHA TOOLS -- using any of these takes this run
     off the leaderboard, permanently. ...");
  2. at first use mid-run, as a WARNING toast naming the turn ("Turning them off
     does not undo this.");
  3. at game over ("NOT RANKED: Alpha Tools were used in this run. Play without
     them for the board.").

**What is gated as an alpha tool (state mutations only):**
- F3 debug overlay: Add \$50k Money, Add 5 Action Points, event injection via the
  Trigger Event popup.
- Backslash overlay (retitled **ALPHA TOOLS**, the ruled player-facing name):
  money/doom/reputation/compute nudges, the forced day-step, queue-selected-event,
  trigger-random-event.

**Deliberately NOT gated:** read-only surfaces (F3 state/errors/performance tabs, the
readout column, hidden risk-pool display), the JUMP navigation buttons, Reset Game
(it starts a NEW run, which is genuinely clean and resets the flag anyway), the
passive dev-build recorders (flight recorder, perf log, UI evolution recorder -- no
gameplay effect), and ordinary settings. Looking is free; touching is not.

## Contradiction left open on purpose: #788

#788 ("mark runs where dev mode was used -- visible badge, NOT exclusion",
ship:hotpatch-48h) proposes the OPPOSITE of this ruling (exclude + warn). Pip has not
reconciled them; this PR implements the card's ruling and **leaves #788 open**. The
card's own recommendation was "exclude now, mark later" -- #788 becomes the better
answer once the board is rich enough that losing entries costs more than ambiguity.

## Drive-by fix (found by the new tests)

debug_overlay.update_game_state() still read state.seed, which GameState renamed to
game_seed_str -- so the F3 Game State tab ABORTED with an invalid-access script error
on every render with a live game. One-line fix, regression-covered by the toggle test.

## Verification

- Baseline (before any edit): quick gate **1031 tests, 0 failures, 101/101 files**.
- After: quick gate **1044 tests, 0 failures, 102/102 files** (delta +13, all in the
  new godot/tests/unit/test_ranked_run_integrity.gd).
- Simulation tier: test_game_manager.gd run directly, **35/35 passed** (its Easy/Hard
  scaling tests now lift the lock via a test-only override seam,
  GameConfig._difficulty_lock_override -- the perf_log override pattern -- since they
  exercise the machinery that returns when the lock lifts).
- **Red-proof (the #1082 lesson, guards demonstrated able to fail):**
  1. reverted consumption to the raw field -> 2 tests failed exactly as predicted
     (Easy grant 24 and Hard grant 16 reached game state); restored -> green.
  2. removed the alpha_tools_used check from is_ranked_run() -> 5 tests failed
     (sticky/reset/overlay/save-load suite); restored -> green.

## Not verified here

- Visual pass on the two warning labels + disabled Settings dropdown (needs eyes on a
  running build; wiring is code-only and unit-covered).
- The Settings merge with feat/settings-operations-board (expected trivial).
- Old-save compatibility exercised only via the .get() default path in unit tests,
  not against a real pre-feature save file.

issues.title: feat(settings): rebuild as front card + operations board -- directions 5 and 1 as one screen (#1096)
issues.body:
## The failure that earned this

The settings screen Pip called "pretty amateur" (2026-08-01 playtest) carried three
instances of silent wrongness:

1. **Apply was a data-loss trap.** Every control applied live but persisted only on
   Apply, so Back-without-Apply silently reverted everything on next launch. The
   standard player mental model ("it changed, so it's saved") lost data here.
2. **The Keyboard Shortcuts grid was stale.** It advertised `[F5] Quick save` /
   `[F9] Quick load`; no F5 binding exists anywhere and F9 is a debug-only layout
   flip. Hand-copied documentation drifting from reality.
3. **The layout shape that hid six shipped sections below a scroll fold** (defused by
   PR #1095) was still the screen's architecture.

## What this builds

Pip's ruling (memo #1096, `docs/SPOKEN_RULINGS_2026-08-02_playtest-and-cards.md`
section 4): **"settings directions 1 and 5 proceed, diegetic deferred until a designer
is hired."** Spec: `docs/design/SETTINGS_MENU_OPTIONS.md`.

Directions 5 and 1 are built as **one scene with a deliberate relationship** -- 5 is the
front, 1 is what sits behind the door:

- **FRONT CARD (Direction 5)** -- default view. Volume, music, fullscreen, gameplay
  hints, colorblind: the five intents nearly every early settings visit is one of, on a
  small centered card. One door: `>> ALL PROTOCOLS` (captioned "sound detail, display,
  privacy, intros, rival feed, experiments"), plus `>> KEYBINDINGS`.
- **OPERATIONS BOARD (Direction 1)** -- behind the door, same scene (a visibility
  toggle, no scene navigation). Every remaining control on one dense three-column
  board grouped by the player's question: Col 1 my machine (AUDIO, DISPLAY), Col 2 my
  game (OPERATIONS, INTERFACE, ACCESS), Col 3 my data + my hands (DISCLOSURE, CONTROLS).
  Header strip carries version + board epoch; **no ScrollContainer exists anywhere in
  the scene**, so no control can ever hide below a fold again. DISCLOSURE gives the
  privacy pair (identity consent, launch ping) their own header and honest sentences
  instead of burying them under "Gameplay". ESC walks back out the way you came:
  board -> front card -> leave.

The duplicated controls (the front-card five also appear on the board, which must stay
a complete audit surface) share one handler each and are re-read from GameConfig on
every view switch.

## Apply: killed, replaced with persist-on-change

Chose **persist-on-change** (0.75s debounced save + flush on every exit path,
`_exit_tree` backstop) over "make Back explicit about discarding" because a discard
dialog keeps the trap open for ESC/alt-F4/window-close exits and adds a modal nobody
reads. Both views state the rule on screen: "changes save automatically", flipping to
"[OK] saved" after a write. The debounce coalesces a slider drag into one disk write.

## Also in here

- **Stale shortcuts grid DELETED**; both views link the real keybind screen
  (profiles + rebinding -- self-maintaining, cannot drift).
- **New board row: "Rival intel in the WATCH feed"** (`show_rivals_feed`) -- a
  persisted preference that previously had UI only on the WATCH screen filter button.
  Adds the missing `set_setting` case in `game_config.gd`. Known seam: a change made
  here mid-run applies on the next feed rebuild, not instantly (nothing listens to
  `config_changed`; the settings screen is normally reached from welcome, so this is
  theoretical outside the dev-overlay jump).
- Live-run reentry guard preserved byte-for-byte (`[BACK TO GAME]` relabel,
  `pending_resume` routing).

## What this deliberately does NOT do

- **Does NOT reinstate the graphics-quality dropdown** (removed in #1095;
  `apply_graphics_settings()` still carries a TODO and reads nothing). A test guards
  against its return until it is wired.
- **Does NOT touch the difficulty write path.** MERGE-ORDER NOTE: the Research
  Intensity row MOVED into the board's OPERATIONS column, but `_on_difficulty_changed`
  is byte-identical to the pre-rebuild handler and the debounced save is attached as a
  separate signal connection. Issue #1084 (`feat/alpha-tools-and-difficulty-lock` lane)
  owns that row's behaviour; whichever lands second will conflict in
  `settings_menu.gd`/`settings_menu.tscn` and should keep #1084's semantics for the
  row. The spec's shared assumption was to remove the row entirely -- left for #1084
  to decide.
- **Does NOT build Direction 3** (diegetic lab floor) -- deferred by ruling until a
  designer is hired.
- **Does NOT put the common early settings on the pause screen** -- Pip's "great
  pickup" from the same capture is a different surface (the pause menu already has
  inline audio sliders); follow-up work.
- **Does NOT fix keybind_screen's Back**, which returns to welcome even when entered
  from settings -- pre-existing seam, worth a small follow-up (return-to-caller).

## Tests

Fast gate in the worktree: **1035 tests / 0 failures / 101 files** vs main baseline
**1031 / 0 / 101** (+4 net). Five old fold-geometry tests hardcoding the dead node
tree were replaced by nine guards restating the same intents against the new
structure: front card default + five intents present, full board inventory (14 named
controls), board fits its frame at the 1080p design viewport, no scroll region
anywhere, no quality control, Apply dead + autosave mechanism armed, stale grid dead.

**Honest limit: tests prove structure and wiring, not that the screen looks right.**
Column balance, card proportions, header icon rendering, and how the board reads at a
glance need Pip's eyes on a running build (preview worktree + `--import` pass per the
usual visual-pass flow).

## What needs Pip's eyes

1. The board's three-column balance and density at 1080p (and any window size he
   actually plays at -- the board is anchored full-rect, not fixed 800x600).
2. Front-card wording: "Volume" (master) vs "Music" split, and the ALL PROTOCOLS
   caption line.
3. Whether "saving... / [OK] saved" footer feedback is enough, or he wants the
   Direction-1 wireframe's "saved 3s ago" timestamp.
4. The persist-on-change ruling itself (vs explicit-discard Back) -- argued above,
   reversible in one function if he disagrees.

issues.title: Review: what does pdoom1 actually want from pdoom-data? (measured inventory, no proposal)
issues.body:
**Raised at Pip's direction** (`pdoom-data#55`): pdoom1 decides what it wants from pdoom-data, and pdoom-data then supplies that. Direction of authority is pdoom1 -> pdoom-data. So this issue carries measurements and questions, and deliberately **no proposal**.

Findings come from a read-only static audit of this repo plus JSON measurement of the corpus. The game was not run; anything runtime-dependent is flagged.

---

## The question

**What do you actually want a pdoom-data event to carry?**

Everything below exists so that can be answered against facts rather than against either side's guesses. If the answer is "much less than we currently send", that is a good outcome and cheap to deliver.

---

## What pdoom1 reads today

`godot/data/historical_events.json`, 1,194 records. Every raw-record access in the tree is in one file, `godot/autoload/event_service.gd`.

**Nine of thirteen fields are read.** Never accessed anywhere: `sources` (1,194 records, none empty), `tags`, `impacts[].condition` (3,636 entries, all null), `source_id`. `pdoom_impact` is copied onto the transformed event and then read by nothing; 1,187 of its 1,194 values are null.

Derived keys written onto the game event that nothing downstream reads: `eligibility_start`, `eligibility_end`, `trigger_mode`, `historical`, `significance`, `source_data` (which carries a full copy of the raw record).

## The number that should shape the answer

**98.3% of the corpus never reaches a decision window.** `_is_flavour_event` (`event_service.gd:491-497`) demotes every `technical_research_breakthrough` and every `arxiv*` id to `delivery_tier: "feed"`. Feed items render as one grey line and **their options are never presented and their effects never applied**.

1,174 of 1,194 records are inert beyond `id`, `title`, `category`, `year`. Twenty can open a window; one is then dropped by the start-year filter.

**So the decision surface pdoom1 gets from 1,194 curated events is nineteen records.**

That is the single most decision-relevant fact in this audit. If pdoom-data is supplying 1,194 records to fill nineteen slots, the contract question is not "which fields" but "which records, and chosen how".

## Rarity is not carrying the meaning your curve file assumes

Corpus: rare 1,076, common 77, legendary 41.

**All 41 `legendary` records are in the arxiv/flavour stream** — so the tier meaning "always fires at its historical date, key story beat" is applied exclusively to records that are then demoted to a grey line. The nineteen records that can open a window are seventeen `common` and three `rare`. **Zero legendary.**

Cause, measured in pdoom-data: `rarity` is an exact `text_length > 20000` threshold on a field that is not carried into the output (`pdoom-data#51`). Zero violations in 1,129 records. Correlation with the visible description length is r = -0.0065.

Boundary case nobody validates: `_get_rarity_settings` tests `_rarity_curves.has(rarity)`, and `rarity_curves.json` has top-level keys `default_rarity`, `year_trigger`, `_description`, `_note`. A record with `rarity: "year_trigger"` would pass that test and return the wrong dict. No such record exists today.

## Significance discriminates almost nothing

`significance` is summed from `abs(change)` across `impacts` and scales every generated option's effects (`event_service.gd:500-528`, `:587-590`).

**1,166 of 1,194 records score exactly 6.** Whole-corpus distribution `{6: 1166, 8: 4, 9: 6, 10: 18}`.

## `impacts` are not inert, and three of your docs say they are

`events.gd:290-310` intercepts a literal `doom` key and reroutes it into `doom_system.add_stream_input("panic", ...)`. Its own comment names **pdoom-data-derived events as the sole remaining producer of literal doom effects**.

`WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md:280-282`, `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md:78-79` and `resource_accessor.gd:73-76` all still describe that path as an inert sink. Flagging as a doc/code disagreement rather than asserting which is intended.

Meanwhile pdoom-data's supplied vocabulary — `vibey_doom`, `stress`, `burnout_risk` — maps onto `doom` via `variable_mapping.json`, which is precisely what ADR-0015 outlaws. It survives only because of that reroute. Three variables are silently dropped as unmapped: `ethics_risk` (16), `technical_debt` (12), `media_reputation` (4). They still count toward significance.

Path B (literal effects) reaches gameplay for **seven records only** — the `funding_catastrophe` branch. The other twelve window-tier records build effects from `significance` alone.

## Three asks already on your record that pdoom-data does not answer

Not new requests from us. These are pdoom1's own documents.

**ADR-0012** (accepted 2026-07-12) names four event-content fields: *class, expiry N, response-expected flag, carrying-cost hook*. pdoom-data supplies none; everything defaults to `deferrable`.

**pdoom1#630 / `UI_FEATURES_STACK.md:39-44`** — the feed drowning in `hist_arxiv`, "the ENTIRE hist_arxiv deck fires, 200+ entries in event_cooldowns". `SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-17.md:36-37` names pdoom-data's salience tiers as the principled fix. pdoom-data has that field on its candidate feed (`salience_tier_by_profile`, A 172 / B 687 / C 1717 / D 858) but **not on `all_events.json`**, which is the collection you read.

**`TRIUMVIRATE_METABOLIC_CYCLE.md:90-116`** (proposed, not ratified) asks for monthly facts-only packs and states the split: *pdoom-data owns the fact schema, pdoom1 owns the shaping schema*. pdoom-data has since ratified its side of that as ADR-007 and ADR-008.

## One thing pdoom-data will not do, and why it is in your interest

DQ-21 is resolved and its vocabulary is live — `general_capability`, `frontier_capability`, `global_compute`, `dedicated_ai_compute`, `political_pressure`, `ambient_risk`, `global_alarm`, `global_panic`, accepted at `events.gd:315-337`. pdoom-data could encode those names directly.

**ADR-007 in pdoom-data says it should not**, and the reason favours you: if we encode `frontier_capability` and you later rename or split it, every exported pack already in the wild silently means the wrong thing — no error, no failed parse, just numbers attached to a concept that no longer exists. An external taxonomy plus a mapping table on your side keeps your vocabulary yours to revise as often as the design needs.

If you would rather have your names directly, say so and we will do it — but that is the trade being made.

## Also outstanding, unrelated to schema

`pdoom1#1098` — 42 records in the bundled copy still carry un-redacted email addresses. `scripts/sync_from_pdoom_data.sh` reads directories that no longer exist in pdoom-data and has never successfully run, so there is no path for upstream corrections to arrive.

## Could not determine

Whether any of this holds at runtime; everything is static tracing plus JSON measurement. Why `historical_events.json` is a hand-commit rather than a sync output. Whether the "inert sink" docs are simply stale post-#985 or describe a path not traced.

Refs `pdoom-data#43`, `pdoom-data#51`, `pdoom-data#52`, `pdoom-data#55`, `pdoom1#630`, `pdoom1#1052`, `pdoom1#1098`, `pdoom1-website#240`.

issues.title: The shipped game contacts api.pdoom.org and would ingest the response unvalidated -- the subdomain does not currently exist
issues.body:
Found 2026-08-02 while ruling on the pdoom-data contract. **Filed for a ruling, not because exploitation is occurring** -- it is not, today. But the shape is bad enough to close deliberately rather than leave.

## What the code does

`godot/autoload/event_service.gd`:

```gdscript
const API_BASE_URL = "https://api.pdoom.org/v1"   # line 26, comment says "Future API endpoint"
...
var url = "%s/events/timeline" % API_BASE_URL      # line 253
var error = http_request.request(url)              # line 257
```

The autoload builds an `HTTPRequest` in `_ready()` and this path fetches a timeline of historical events. **The response is ingested with no schema validation** (established by the agent that traced the consumption path; I have not independently re-read every line of the ingest).

## What I measured just now

```
pdoom.org       -> 185.199.108.153, .109.153, .110.153, .111.153   (GitHub Pages)
api.pdoom.org   -> NXDOMAIN, does not resolve
pdoom1.com      -> 173.236.253.218                                  (DreamHost, ours)
GET https://api.pdoom.org/v1/events/timeline -> HTTP 000, connection failed
```

Three things follow:

1. **It is inert today.** The subdomain does not exist, the request fails, nothing is ingested. No current exposure.
2. **`pdoom.org` is a DIFFERENT DOMAIN from `pdoom1.com`**, and it resolves to GitHub Pages. Our own infrastructure is `pdoom1.com` / `api.pdoom1.com`.
3. **The score API this project actually uses is `api.pdoom1.com`**, not `api.pdoom.org`. These are not the same host.

## The question that decides severity, and only Pip can answer it

**Do we control `pdoom.org`?**

- **If yes:** this is dead config pointing at a subdomain we never created. Low severity, still worth removing.
- **If no:** every shipped binary makes a DNS lookup for a subdomain on a domain someone else controls. The day that party adds an `api` record, our released clients begin fetching JSON from them and feeding it into the event system without validation. That is a supply-chain path into every installed copy, opened by a constant nobody has looked at since it was written as a placeholder -- the comment literally says *"Future API endpoint"*.

**A domain we do not own, contacted by shipped software, parsing whatever comes back, is not a thing to leave open because it currently 404s.**

## Recommended fix, independent of the answer

1. **Remove or hard-disable the fetch.** It has never worked -- the subdomain has never existed -- so nothing regresses. The local snapshot (`godot/data/historical_events.json`, a one-time 2025-12-25 export) is what the game actually runs on.
2. If a remote timeline is wanted later, point it at **`api.pdoom1.com`**, infrastructure we own, and **validate the response against a schema before ingest**. An unvalidated remote ingest is the same failure family as #1027: the data renders, nothing errors, and the content is whatever someone else decided.
3. Whatever the answer on ownership, **register or lock down `api.pdoom1.com`'s naming convention** so a future placeholder cannot drift onto a third-party domain again.

## Related, found in the same pass and worth its own issues

- `rarity_curves.json` assumes **52 turns/year**, the Clock runs ~**260 workday-turns/year**, and a code fallback says **12**. So "events fire on their historical dates" is currently false regardless of any data contract.
- `docs/data/HISTORICAL_DATA_INTEGRATION.md`, `sync_from_pdoom_data.sh` and `timeline_loader.gd` describe a second ingest pipeline with **zero callers**. Dead docs that will mislead the next contract discussion.
- 54 pre-2017 records can never fire.

See `docs/decision-cards/2026-08-02_pdoom-data-contract.md` for the full field-level inventory.

issues.title: feat(month-review): show what CHANGED, and let SPACE open the door (A1/A4/A10/B1/B2/B3)
issues.body:
Pip ruled the whole month-review pack on 2026-08-02 (#1096): "month-review A1-A10 and
B1-B5 with A6 deferred." This is the unambiguous, low-risk half. The structural half and
the data-capture half are named below and deliberately NOT here.

Lead with the failures, because each change is one.

-- A1. The review told him things he was already looking at. --

At [3:45], reading `Funds: $84,200 | Doom: 31.2% | Staff: 3`: "funds is good, but I CAN
SEE THAT UP HERE, so this is NOT FRESH INFORMATION." He is right, and it is worse than
redundant: a screen that opens every month and spends its best line restating the top bar
teaches the player that the screen is skippable. The level line is deleted. The top bar
owns funds, the doom meter owns doom, the roster owns staff.

-- A4. What the HUD cannot show is MOVEMENT, so that is now all the review prints. --

`Funds $102,000 -> $84,200 (-$17,800)`, `Staff 3 -> 4 (+1)`, and doom as BAND movement.
Only stats that actually moved get a line: "Funds unchanged" would be exactly the
non-fresh information A1 just deleted, in different words. A quiet month therefore prints
no movement block at all, which is the honest output and is the accepted cost the options
doc flagged (the review gets thinner before A2/A3 give it new content).

Doom is band-only -- `ELEVATED -> HIGH (crossed up)`, via ThemeManager's canonical band
labels, the same non-color channel the HUD already uses. No percentage, no per-cause
attribution. ADR-0015 makes doom a computed consequence of world state, so a printed
per-source number would assert the retired "single source-destination number bump" model;
per-cause attribution stays behind the paid doom-breakdown instrument (ADR-0001,
spending-buys-sight). A start/end band comparison is world-state display and is legal.
Two tests pin that no "%" can ever reach that string.

The measurement point is not obvious and is the one genuinely subtle thing here.
MonthController.advance_tick() runs _open_plan_month() -- which charges the NEW month's
office rent -- BEFORE _finish_month_playback() builds the review. Reading state.money at
render time would therefore book next month's rent against last month's funds delta,
every month, in the same direction, and it would look plausible. So the end-of-month
reading is taken immediately BEFORE each day tick (_last_tick_stats); when a tick turns
out to be the boundary, that reading is the true last day of the old month. The baseline
for the NEXT review is taken after the popup is built. Both readings are display-only:
no RNG, no writes, determinism and replay untouched.

The movement baseline is not serialized. A loaded save shows no movement block on its
first review and resumes normally -- degrade quietly rather than print a delta measured
against a month the player did not play.

-- A10. Dismissing the review destroyed the only copy of it. --

[3:49] "it's actually just kind of popping up and blocking the screen." Half of why
blocking feels bad is the read-now-or-lose-it pressure: the popup was the sole copy.
Every review now also lands in the WATCH feed as a compact block, so closing it costs
nothing and months can be compared by scrolling back. New channel "review", which the
existing feed filters cannot suppress (they hide only "flavour", the arxiv flood, and
"rivals", the intel toggle) -- a review can never be silently swallowed.

This is a palliative, not the fix. A5 -- the review as a dismissible panel, or docked into
the plan screen so it informs the decisions it is about -- is the structural answer and is
not in this PR.

-- B1. The two keys every player tries first did nothing. --

main_ui.gd's _input blocks SPACE and ENTER outright whenever any dialog is up. That rule
is correct and stays: it stops an accidental end-turn or commit landing on a crisis
window. But no exception existed for a popup that is not a decision, so the month review
-- a door with one costless option -- ate both keys, and the key that DID work (Q) worked
only because "Begin planning..." happened to be button 0 in the letter map. Pip found Q by
accident at [4:55].

His ruling at [4:55]-[5:03]: "maybe a space bar or something as well -- maybe not enter,
if enter is going to be the commit turn thing, we don't want people doing that
accidentally." Implemented exactly. EventDialog sets a "space_advances" meta on a
one-costless-option popup; MainUI.dialog_key_advances() promotes SPACE past the block for
that dialog and nothing else. ENTER returns false unconditionally and there is no meta
that can change it -- if dismissing a monthly popup trained ENTER as a "next" reflex,
players would start committing turns by muscle memory, which is the exact accident he
named. SPACE is also semantically consistent: outside dialogs SPACE already means "advance
the loop".

dialog_key_advances is static and takes the dialog and the keycode, so the whole decision
is unit-testable without instantiating the 3k-line MainUI or a live input stack.

-- B2. The door had a price tag. --

It rendered `[Q] Begin planning August 2017 (Free)`. The `(Free)` is
format_cost_summary({}), a deliberate 2026-07-24 fix for crisis OPTIONS where a blank cost
read as ambiguous -- correct there, nonsense on navigation. The `[Q]` is an arbitrary index
into dialog_key_labels, not a considered binding. Both are suppressed for a
one-costless-option popup and replaced with the key the player actually reaches for:
`Begin planning August 2017   [SPACE]`. Free-ness is decided by asking format_cost_summary
what it WOULD have printed, so the predicate can never drift from the chrome it suppresses
(there is a test pinning that too). The letter key still WORKS -- it is only unadvertised.

-- B3. The forward door looked half-disabled. --

Dark-gray 500x45, identical to any event option, while the loop's other primary action
(END TURN) is teal and 16px. The two doors of the month loop did not look like siblings,
and a dark-gray button next to grayed-out unaffordable options reads as disabled. The
navigation button now takes the END TURN teal (0.118, 0.765, 0.702 -- lifted from
scenes/main.tscn), 16px, 520x54, teal border on a dark teal fill. Deliberately not a flat
teal block: the review text sits on the same panel and a saturated fill would out-shout
the thing it is meant to close.

-- What this PR does NOT do, and why --

A2, A3 and A9 are NOT here even though Pip approved them. They all need a pre-reset
snapshot first: MonthPlan.begin_month() RESETS attention_spent, attention_reserved,
reserve_used, hours_spent and kind_spent one call before the review renders. His [3:24]
"I don't see what my unspent reserve here WAS" is not a layout gap -- the number does not
exist at render time. That is a data-capture change with its own save/load and ordering
questions, and it belongs in its own PR where it can be reviewed as one. A2's snapshot is
the substrate A3 and A9 render from, so they follow it.

A6 (the month as a headline) is deferred by Pip's own ruling.
A5b (docking the review into the plan screen) and B5 (deleting the button) are structural.
A7/A8 (introducing rivals before reporting them) is issue #1088, a separate lane.
B4 (putting the fresh Attention number on the door) was not in scope for this pass.

-- Verification --

Fast gate in this worktree: 1031 tests / 101 files before, 1055 tests / 103 files after,
0 failures both times. The +24 are the two new suites: test_month_review_navigation.gd
(SPACE/ENTER routing and the navigation-popup predicate -- routing is behaviour, so it is
testable) and test_month_review_movement.gd (movement rendering, the omit-unchanged rule,
and the ADR-0015 no-percentage guard).

Honest limit: nothing here proves the screen LOOKS right. The teal weighting, the thinner
body and the [SPACE] hint need Pip's eyes in a running build.

issues.title: fix(release): derive export filename from the preset, and publish the Linux alias (#1072, #1068)
issues.body:
Two release-pipeline defects. Both cheap now, both get expensive as patch cadence rises.

## FOR THE WEBSITE REPO -- the name to point at

**`PDoom-Linux.zip`**

```
https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/releases/latest/download/PDoom-Linux.zip
```

That is the name `docs/RELEASE_PLATFORMS.md` already prescribed, and it matches the shape Windows already uses (`PDoom-Windows.zip`). It starts existing on the **next release cut** -- this PR changes the producer, not the already-published v0.13.2 assets. The current button points at `PDoom.x86_64`, which has never been an asset.

Why not publish a bare `PDoom.x86_64` to match the existing button? Because it would be a broken download: without the sibling `PDoom.pck` and the GodotSteam `.so` libraries it cannot run. That is exactly why the other two platforms ship zips.

## Fix 1 -- #1072: hardcoded output name

`tools/build_release.py` computed `exe_path = out_dir / "PDoom.exe"` regardless of `--preset`. Linux and macOS exports landed named `PDoom.exe` (observed: the Linux build landed at `builds/linux/x11/PDoom.exe`), and three presets sharing one `--output` would silently overwrite each other. For a tool whose entire purpose is proving which source produced which binary, a silent cross-platform overwrite is squarely against the point.

The filename now comes from the chosen preset's own `export_path` in `godot/export_presets.cfg` (`output_name_for_preset`). One source of truth that cannot drift from what a manual export produces; a hardcoded platform map would drift.

Implementation note worth knowing: `export_presets.cfg` is INI-*shaped* but not INI -- the macOS preset carries multi-line unindented dict values (`application/copyright_localized={...}`) that `configparser` rejects. So the parser is a line-wise scanner reading only top-level `[preset.N]` sections, deliberately ignoring `[preset.N.options]` (a stray `export_path` in the options sub-section must not redirect the build; there is a test for that).

### Adjacent, same pass: the zipped-bundle false failure

The freshness check grepped the output's raw bytes for the marker token. Inside a macOS `.app.zip` the marker filename sits in a **compressed** `.pck` entry, not the zip's plaintext central directory -- so it would have reported a FALSE FAILURE on macOS.

`find_marker()` now descends into zip containers: entry names first (cheap), then entry contents, streamed in 1 MiB chunks with a carry-over tail so a match straddling a chunk boundary is still found (packs are hundreds of MB).

**The check was not weakened.** A zip genuinely lacking the marker still fails loudly; `--no-clean` is still the wrong answer to a `[BUILD-VERIFY]` failure. There is a test asserting a marker-free zip still reports absent. That guarantee cost ~12 cycles in v0.11.0 to learn was necessary.

## Fix 2 -- #1068: the site's Linux download 404s

Measured against live v0.13.2: `PDoom-Windows.zip` 200, `PDoom.app.zip` 200, `PDoom.x86_64` **404**.

`scripts/build_all_platforms.py` now emits `PDoom-Linux.zip` alongside `PDoom-Linux-v<X.Y.Z>.zip`, using the same `shutil.copy2` alias step Windows already had. `enhanced-release.yml` already uploads `build-linux/**/*.zip`, so no upload-glob change is needed.

An asset-naming convention applied to two of three platforms is not a convention; it is two special cases.

## Why "Verify Release Download URLs" passed green on a dead URL

Cheap to see, so here it is. That job runs `scripts/verify_release_urls.py --file public/releases/<version>.json` -- it checks the URLs the generated **feed** lists, and the feed's `downloads` block lists **versioned** zips only (`PDoom-Linux-v0.13.2.zip`, which does resolve). The website's buttons are a second, independent path: fixed strings against `releases/latest/download/<name>`. Those unversioned aliases were never in the feed, so were never checked. The proxy ("the checked downloads work") had detached from the thing ("the downloads people actually click work").

Closed here: a blocking step that asserts all three alias assets exist. It checks **by tag**, not `latest`, deliberately -- `latest` may not have flipped yet when the job runs, and a prerelease never becomes Latest at all, so a `latest`-based check would be flaky in one direction and blind in the other.

I did not touch the feed generator to add `*_latest` URLs. That would have been the other way to close it, but it changes the feed schema the website consumes and would go stale against every already-published release (no old release has a Linux alias), fighting the `release-index-check` hook. Flagging as a possible follow-up, not doing it here.

## Tests

`tests/test_build_release_paths.py` -- 19 unit tests over the pure logic (`python -m unittest tests.test_build_release_paths`, all pass):

- preset parsing: ordering, the options-subsection trap, the multi-line dict value that breaks `configparser`
- name derivation: all three platforms, distinctness, Windows backslashes, bare filename, unknown preset, empty/missing `export_path`
- **against the real `godot/export_presets.cfg`**, so the derivation cannot drift from what ships
- `find_marker`: plain file hit/miss, chunk-boundary straddle, a real DEFLATEd zip whose token is provably absent from the container's raw bytes (the macOS shape), marker-as-entry-name, and marker-free zip still failing

Godot fast gate in the worktree, **1031 tests / 0 failures before and after** -- no delta, and none expected: no `.gd` was touched.

Also refreshed `docs/RELEASE_PLATFORMS.md`, which documented both defects as live hazards.

## Out of scope, deliberately

- **#1069** -- the release pipeline builds its own assets, bypassing `build_release.py`'s freshness proof. Bigger; needs a ruling from Pip on which of three options.
- **#1071** -- macOS never verified to run. Needs a human with a Mac, not code.

Refs #1072, #1068.

Do not merge without review.

issues.title: ADR-0015 / DQ-21: what should a pdoom-data event carry, now that literal doom fields are deprecated?
issues.body:
From pdoom-data. Two questions, one blocking and one design-level. Read-only investigation on our side; no changes made to pdoom1.

## Context

pdoom-data ships `event_v1` records carrying `impacts: [{variable, change}]`, `rarity` and `pdoom_impact`. **ADR-0015 (accepted 2026-07-13) deprecates exactly that shape:**

> No action or event definition carries a literal doom field. Effects target intermediary world-state variables ... doom is computed from world state each day tick.

So our schema is currently handing you the "single source-destination number bumps" that ADR names as legacy. We want to stop doing that. We do **not** want to guess our way to a replacement, because ADR-0015 point 2 says adding an intermediary is an ADR-grade act — and inventing your mechanical vocabulary from outside your repo would be exactly the wrong move.

We also found two candidate vocabularies and could not tell which is live:

| Source | Vocabulary |
|---|---|
| ADR-0015 examples, marked "v1 vocabulary owed, DQ-21" | lab capability, deployment pressure, governance quality, public salience |
| `godot/docs/design/RISK_SYSTEM.md` (2025-12-25, "In Development") | Capability Overhang, Research Integrity, Regulatory Attention, Public Awareness, Insider Threat, Financial Exposure |

## Question 1 (blocking us)

**What is DQ-21's status and rough timeline?** We have a consumer-facing export profile blocked on it (pdoom-data#43). Blocked is the correct state — we are not looking to route around it — but knowing whether it is weeks or months changes what we build meanwhile.

Also: is `RISK_SYSTEM.md` superseded by ADR-0015, or are the six risk pools the intended v1 intermediaries under a different name?

## Question 2 (the design one)

**What do you actually want an event to carry?**

Our current thinking is that the answer might be "nothing mechanical at all" — that events cross the boundary as facts plus clearly-attributed editorial opinion, and every mechanical consequence is computed inside pdoom1. That would be the cleanest version of the firewall either repo has managed, and it would make our export profile simpler rather than harder.

If you do want a directional hint, our proposal is that it should be expressed **in a vocabulary pdoom-data owns and can defend** — for example the MIT AI Risk Repository domains we already tag against, plus a direction and a confidence — rather than in your internal variable names. You would keep a mapping table from our stable taxonomy onto your intermediaries.

The reason is deliberately in your interest: it means DQ-21 can change, and change again, **without churning our data**. Only your mapping table moves. Standard anti-corruption layer between two bounded contexts. If instead we encoded your intermediaries directly, every vocabulary revision would require a schema version bump and a re-export on our side, and stale copies in the wild would silently mean the wrong thing.

## A framing we would like to adopt from you

ADR-0015 point 4 states our boundary better than our own docs do:

> The doom function is structure; intermediary pricing is numbers ... MtG framing: events are cards, the doom function is the rules.

We propose adopting that verbatim in pdoom-data's glossary rather than maintaining a parallel vocabulary. pdoom-data ships cards; pdoom1 owns the rules. Object if that misrepresents the intent.

## Related

- pdoom-data#43 — export profile, blocked on this
- pdoom-data#34 — moving pdoom1's resource model out of our shared schema
- pdoom-data#27 — Hop A ratification, where the monthly World-Update Pack was agreed
- pdoom1#962 — frontier-labs integration (unblocked, dataset shipped)

issues.title: PII: 42 records in godot/data/historical_events.json still carry un-redacted email addresses
issues.body:
**Raised from the pdoom-data seat. Ships with the game, so flagging before anything else.**

`godot/data/historical_events.json` contains **42 records carrying un-redacted email addresses** in their `description` field. These are contact addresses printed on academic papers, pulled in by an unparsed-PDF-text import. They belong to real people who did not consent to being in a game's dataset.

pdoom-data fixed this at source on 2026-08-02 (pdoom-data#50). **pdoom1's copy did not receive the fix**, because it is a hand-commit from 2025-12-25 (`88a71959`) and nothing syncs it.

## Measured

Diffing pdoom1's copy against `pdoom-data/data/serveable/api/timeline_events/all_events.json`:

```
same 1194 ids, zero adds, zero removes
records differing: 42
fields that differ: [('description', 42)]
records where pdoom-data contains a redaction marker: 42 of 42
pdoom1 records with an email-like string, whole file: 42
pdoom-data, same check:                                0
```

Every one of the 42 differences is a redaction present upstream and absent here. There is no other drift between the two copies.

## The fix

Copy the current `all_events.json` from pdoom-data over `godot/data/historical_events.json`. The files are otherwise identical, so the diff is exactly the 42 redactions and nothing else — no schema change, no id change, no behaviour change.

I have deliberately not done this myself: it is your repo and your bundled asset. Say the word and I will open the PR, or take it directly.

## What this does not fix, and the decision it implies

Redaction applies to HEAD only. The addresses remain in this repo's git history, in any clone, and in any built artefact already distributed. That is the same limitation pdoom-data has, and the same open question: whether a history rewrite is warranted. Pip has recorded that as **LATER** for pdoom-data (pdoom-data#55 A3). If pdoom1 has shipped builds containing this file, the calculus here may differ from pdoom-data's, because a distributed build cannot be rewritten at all.

## The structural cause, which matters more than the instance

**There is no working pipeline from pdoom-data to pdoom1.** `scripts/sync_from_pdoom_data.sh` reads `$PDOOM_DATA_REPO/transformed/` and `/cleaned/`, neither of which exists in pdoom-data's current layout (`data/raw|transformed|serveable`), and it never touches `historical_events.json` at all. It has never successfully run. The bundled copy is a one-time hand-commit.

So this will happen again with the next upstream correction, silently, and nobody will know until someone diffs the two files. A fix at the data source does not reach the game.

That is the same shape as the finding that produced pdoom-data#50 in the first place: pdoom1-website had added redaction to *its own output* on 2026-07-29 while the source still carried the addresses. Three copies of one corpus, each fixed separately or not at all.

Related: pdoom-data#52 establishes that `all_events.json` has **no reproducible producer** in any repository, which is the upstream half of the same problem — the file cannot be rebuilt, so it cannot be corrected except by hand-editing, in every repo that holds a copy.

Refs pdoom-data#50, pdoom-data#52, pdoom-data#55, pdoom1-website#220.

issues.title: Pip's rulings, 2026-08-02 -- velocity portfolio weights, and a review pdoom-data is waiting on
issues.body:
Spoken rulings, transcribed on-device. Not re-read by Pip.

## Velocity reconstruction -- his method, then his numbers

He deliberately changed how he used the document: he covered the estimator-method column, looked only at the hours each method produced, and then asked himself how he would **split a 100% portfolio of bets** on which method a future omniscient account would vindicate. The percentages were arrived at **after** one full pass, and the inline comments were written during the first pass -- so where they conflict, the percentages are later and better.

**League week:** A 8%, B 40%, C 6%, D 40%, E 6%.
**Last 14 days:** A 10%, B 40%, C 2%, D 35%, E 3%, F 10%.
**Ranked 1 (most bought) to 6:** A 1, B 2, E 3, C 4, D 5, F 6.

Note the tension worth examining rather than smoothing: B and D split the league-week portfolio almost evenly at 40/40, but on the ranking D falls to fifth. His own annotation asks whether he is *"Brier-ing"* -- treating it as a calibration exercise -- and he judged the exercise *"feels right/correct to be doing."*

He wants **ISO week translated into actual calendar weeks** in future renderings; ISO is the right standard but not the readable one. He confirms the shape: December, then near-silence until scattered touches in February and March, early June, a real push through June, exploding through July.

**Double tick, full agreement, on "the number that matters most."**

## A review pdoom-data is waiting on

`pdoom-data#51` (rarity is a length threshold on a discarded field) and `#52` (`all_events.json` has no producer) predate the workshop-3 decisions. Pip's ruling is that **pdoom1 reviews these findings and decides what information it actually wants from pdoom-data**, which then draws it down -- rather than pdoom-data fixing them unilaterally. Direction of authority runs pdoom1 -> pdoom-data. Filed on their side as `pdoom-data#55`.

## Postmortem

He agrees the slack hour paid for eleven findings and wants it **doubled to two hours**, with the launch schedule recast now that real time-logs exist -- worked through iteratively with him, presented as a couple of different models rather than one plan.

He also singled out a line from the postmortem input for keeping: *"You can audit for it. You cannot audit for a metaphor."* His words: capture that as a keeper.

`pdoom1#1095` -- he will read it Sunday evening or Monday morning, not today.

issues.title: Postmortem input: week of 2026-07-28 and the league-launch effort (outside vantage)
issues.body:
Contributed for the week-of-2026-07-28 postmortem and the league-launch retro. Written from an outside vantage: I spent Friday 31 July in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` doing daily-ops tooling, and observed `pdoom1` / `pdoom1-website` only through live endpoint probes, the GitHub API, and local clones. Weight it accordingly — I did not see the game work from the inside.

One item is deliberately omitted and tracked privately in `coordination`; it is a security matter that should not be described in a public repo until it is closed.

---

## 1. The week's dominant failure mode was absence of signal, not wrong signal

Three independent instances, same shape:

- **`api.pdoom1.com` returned 502 from roughly 28 July until at least 09:00 Sat 1 August.** Nothing announced it. It was found by human eyeball on the 29th and was still 502 four days later. There was no monitor on `/api/health`.
- **A scheduled-task registration script in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` had never once executed.** It contained nested double quotes inside `$()` inside a double-quoted string, which PowerShell 5.1 cannot parse (PowerShell 7 can). It failed at *parse* time, so no task was ever created and nothing surfaced the failure. It looked written, and was therefore assumed done.
- **The ops dashboard itself was three days stale** before anyone regenerated it.

In each case the failed state was indistinguishable from the working state from outside. That is one structural problem wearing three costumes, and it is cheaper to fix than any of the individual bugs.

**Concrete ask:** an uptime check on `https://api.pdoom1.com/api/health` at a 5-minute interval with an email alert. Ten minutes of work. It converts a four-day outage into a five-minute one.

## 2. Score submission during the outage — a hypothesis that needs one person to confirm or kill

If the score API was 502 for four days, every in-game submission in that window hit a dead endpoint. Whether those scores are **lost** or merely **invisible** depends entirely on client behaviour: does the game spool failed submissions and retry, or fire-and-forget?

I have not verified this — I did not read the submission path. But it is a one-file check, it decides whether four days of player scores are recoverable, and it compounds with the already-known `(seed, game_version)` board-key drift, where a mis-versioned score lands nowhere silently.

If the client does not spool, that is a data-durability bug independent of the outage, and the outage merely revealed it.

## 3. Written checklists rotted inside 48 hours

A traffic-readiness checklist written 29 July was re-checked against live state on 31 July. Of its items:

- the stale-homepage-version item had been fixed by someone else (`pdoom1-website#225`)
- two PRs listed as "to merge" had already merged (`pdoom1-website#193`, `pdoom1-website#181`)
- "ship v0.11.0" was obsolete — v0.13.1 had shipped on 26 July
- one security item, "`api.pdoom1.com` has no valid TLS cert", was **simply false**. Direct check: Let's Encrypt certificate, CN matches, valid 8 Jul → 6 Oct, chain verifies

Roughly half the list was wrong within two days, and the wrongness pointed at real work — someone acting on it would have gone to issue a certificate that already existed.

**Suggestion:** stop writing status into prose. Anything that can be probed should be probed at read time. A checklist that asserts state is a cache with no invalidation.

## 4. On working in parallel

Ten PRs were open on `pdoom1-website` with agents still producing overnight, while the one item on the critical path for a league launch — a dead score API — sat untouched for three days.

The parallel work was not wasted. `pdoom1-website#225`, `#193`, `#181`, `#221` and `#223` all landed inside a day, and the public surface is materially better than it was on Monday. `#193` in particular removed 75 academics' email addresses from a public page, which was worth doing on its own.

What was missing was any marker distinguishing *critical path* from *in flight*. Everything sat in one undifferentiated queue, so the loudest item won rather than the blocking one. The fix is not less parallelism — it is one explicitly named blocking item at a time, with everything else labelled as deferred rather than merely un-started.

## 5. The launch did not fire, and that should be recorded as a decision

`public/data/analytics/annotations.json` still holds a single event: friends-and-family alpha links, 22 July. The prep was extensive and the go/no-go criteria were written down, but no share was posted.

Given `pdoom1-website#186` (the 1200x630 OG share card) was in a conflicting state and the score API was down, **not** sharing was the correct call. But nothing in the record says it was a call. If it is not written down as a decision, it reads next week as a failure, and the next launch inherits the wrong lesson.

## 6. Errors of mine, for completeness

- I printed a status sheet asserting that a scheduled task was registered *before* running the registration — which then failed. The paper was briefly wrong. Verify, then print the claim.
- I built an evening runsheet on a 15:45 start; it was read at ~17:20. I scheduled against wall-clock instead of against time-from-pickup, which is the wrong clock for anyone working off paper asynchronously.
- I referred to issues as bare `#186`, `#193` and so on throughout Friday's printed material. `coordination/PRINT_AND_PROCESS_REFERENCE.md` explicitly requires repo-qualified references because a bare number costs a context switch to resolve. This issue uses qualified references throughout.
- I built print tooling in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` on 31 July without checking whether a convention already existed. It did not exist yet at the time, but `coordination` has since documented that at least three repos independently built print and dictation tooling that same day, two of them independently fixing the same focus-stealing bug hours apart. My implementation was a fourth divergence and needs to be reconciled to the canonical settings, not kept.

## Suggested actions out of this

1. Uptime monitor on the score API health endpoint — 5-minute interval, email alert.
2. Confirm or kill the score-spooling hypothesis in section 2. If scores are dropped on submission failure, open a separate durability issue.
3. Record the not-launching decision explicitly, with its reasons, so the retro reads it as judgement.
4. Rebase `pdoom1-website#186` before the next share attempt rather than during it.
5. Reconcile `pipfoweraker-dashboard`'s print path to `coordination/PRINT_AND_PROCESS_REFERENCE.md`.

issues.title: ADR set: correctness/staleness/cohesion pass, and an implementation-status field the website can render
issues.body:
Raised by Pip 2026-07-31, from the website side, after a honesty sweep found that the
website's published rendering of these ADRs makes claims the ADRs themselves do not
support.

## Why this is urgent-ish rather than tidy-up

`pdoom1-website` renders 17 of these ADRs to **public pages** at
`https://pdoom1.com/design-notes/`, via `scripts/sync/sync-design-notes.py`. The
generator wraps every page in framing text that reads:

> These are the actual decision records the game is built from … They describe *why*
> the game works the way it does.

That framing is **present tense and uniform**, and it is false for at least three:

- **ADR-0005** (emergent waves / seed schedules) is published as live design, but
  pdoom1#1020 states: *"ADR-0005 seed schedules are INERT in real play: nothing passes a
  schedule to GameState, so `event_schedule` is always empty."* The page even tells a
  player that *"the turn-9 funding wave on this week's seed becomes community
  vocabulary"* — a mechanic that does not fire. A league player could plan around it.
- **ADR-0003** (Liability Ledger) appears in the roadmap under *"Further out — wanted,
  not scheduled"*.
- **ADR-0007**'s own status says *build **third**, strictly after ADR-0003 and ADR-0004* —
  i.e. not built.

The website will fix its own framing. But the underlying question is yours: **which of
these records describe shipped behaviour, and which describe intent?** Nothing in the
current format distinguishes them, so no downstream consumer can either.

## What Pip is asking for

1. **A correctness / staleness / cohesion pass over the whole ADR set.** For each:
   is it accurate today, superseded, partially implemented, or aspirational?
2. **A machine-readable implementation status.** The website already renders the
   `Status:` line verbatim, so an added field — e.g. `Implemented: yes | partial | no` —
   would let the published page say `ACCEPTED — not yet implemented` automatically,
   with no website change beyond reading one field. This is the smallest fix that
   removes the whole class.
3. **Vocabulary drift.** ADR-0011 describes *"Current build: one global AP pool"* — the
   AP pool has since been removed for the attention economy (pdoom1#1037 is already
   sweeping stale AP wording). "Current build" is unambiguously present tense on a page
   dated three weeks ago. Consider a convention: never write *"current build"* in a
   record that outlives the build.
4. **Publication pipeline.** `sync-design-notes.yml` renders from the latest **release
   tag**, so ADR-0018 (on `main` since 2026-07-27) is not published and a reader cannot
   tell. That is defensible, but it is undocumented. Decide and document: do design
   notes track `main` or the last release? Then make the rendered page state which.

## Cross-repo note

`docs/PLAN_EVENT_INTEGRATION.md` still describes `historical_events.json` as
*"20 events, OLD format"* — it now holds 1,194. And `CHANGELOG.md` has no mention of
`pdoom-data`, `historical_events` or `EventService` at all, so the integration that
~2,190 published website pages describe is undocumented in the game's own changelog.
Worth folding into the same pass.

Filed from pdoom1-website so it is not lost. Happy to take any part of this on the
website side.

issues.title: ui(layout): the Plan screen wastes its middle and scatters its text -- legibility-first layout brief
issues.body:
Captured via the **F6 flight recorder** during a 2026-07-30 16:44 session, at turn 1 with a fresh state (doom 20.0, $245,000) -- so this is explicitly the **new-player opening view**, not a late-game screen. Screenshot and full `state.json` are in the capture:

`%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\P(Doom)\flight_recorder\session_20260730_164411\`

Pip's note, verbatim and unedited, because it reads as a coherent brief rather than a bug list:

> "The vertical stack of buttons should be arranged such that the player doesn't need to scroll to see anything from a starting perspective. The upgrades on the right hand side need to have a vertical column to go up and down like the buttons on the left. We can try having them mirror the icon button stacks but with their vertical slice extending to the top of the screen as well, experiment with wireframing other locations, and consider what parts of the simulation we want to have persistently visible across both Plan and Watch screens, if any. If we don't want to put them on the Plan space, we should workshop UI improvements to the middle of the screen, which is wasted dead space. We can prioritise increasing legibility, particularly legibility for new players. The amount of scattered text over the screen is hard to read for older players, and more instructions should be more intuitive and we should have one more centralised location for text and not otherwise clutter the screen up too much with it. It's not obvious how to progress or end the turn, these things should be spelled out for new players explicitly within the first turn's setup / suggested setup."

## The distinct asks inside it

1. **No scrolling at the opening view.** The left button stack must fit without scrolling from a standing start.
2. **Upgrades need their own vertical column** on the right, scrollable like the left stack -- candidate treatment is mirroring the left icon stack with the vertical slice running to the top of the screen.
3. **Wireframe alternatives before committing.** Explicitly an experiment, not a chosen design.
4. **Decide what stays persistently visible across Plan and Watch.** This is a screen-architecture question, not a layout tweak, and it should be answered before (2) is built -- it changes what the columns are even for.
5. **The middle of the screen is wasted dead space.** Either it earns its area or the flanking columns should claim it. Pip flagged the same thing in the morning playtest: *"the buttons on the left-hand side of the screen I find was to have all this wasted space in the middle"* (#1041, [2:37]).
6. **Legibility first, new players first.** Scattered text across the whole screen is hard to read. Consolidate to fewer, more central text locations; stop cluttering.
7. **How to progress / end the turn is not obvious.** It should be stated explicitly in the first turn's setup or a suggested-setup flow.

## Why this is one issue rather than seven

Items 1, 2, 4 and 5 are all the same question -- what the Plan screen's columns are FOR, and therefore where they live and how wide they are. Fixing them piecemeal produces a layout that is locally better and globally incoherent. Item 4 in particular is upstream of the rest.

Items 6 and 7 are a separate axis (legibility and onboarding) but land on the same surface, so they should be designed together rather than sequentially.

## Related

- #1041 -- the morning playtest's UI findings, including the same dead-middle observation and the hiring/leaderboard screens wanting more room
- #1029 -- intro replay, needed to iterate on item 7 at all without deleting a config value by hand each time
- #814 -- progressive disclosure onboarding (operator monologue, greyed-UI intro, hire waterfall)
- #889 -- Architecture Week / `main_ui.gd` monolith, which is where a real layout rework would have to live

Not for the league. This is design work, and the note itself says "experiment" and "workshop".

## Process note

This capture is the first use of the F6 flight recorder as an actual feedback channel, and it worked exactly as intended: one keypress produced a screenshot, the full serialized game state, and a typed note, all timestamped together. Considerably better evidence than a video frame plus a transcript. Worth keeping as the standard for design observations, with recorded video reserved for things that need motion.

issues.title: art(review): generation was paid for and the outputs were never reviewed -- inventory the backlog and package a decision session
issues.body:
From the recorded playtest of v0.13.2, 2026-08-01 09:52 (`art_generated/audiodump/2026-08-01_09-52-08.transcript.md`, local-only).

## Observation

**[10:04]** "I am also thinking now that I want to just do a big bunch of art reviewing. So I'd also just like to be reminded where that's at and then like maybe I can go make a few hundred decisions. **I think I spent a bunch of money and then like haven't actually kind of seen the outputs from it as well.** So I feel like that's also a pretty big like if we package this we can get this shipped."

The failure shape: generation spend is flowing (and policy says keep it flowing), but the REVIEW half of the loop -- Pip looking at outputs and saying yes/no -- has fallen behind, so paid-for assets sit unreviewed and unshipped. This is the choke point Pip named at [12:27] in general form: "I'm not actually constrained by effort here, I'm constrained by choice."

## Ask

1. **Inventory first**: enumerate every generated-but-unreviewed batch (gpt-image-1 runs under `art_generated/` / `tools/assets` outputs, pixellab jobs, the endgame poster batch #1024 if regenerated) with counts and dates. "Remind me where that's at" is literally the ask -- Pip does not currently know the size of the backlog, and neither does the repo.
2. **Package a decision session**: one local HTML review gallery (repo-resident, per his standing local-tools preference) covering the whole backlog, batched for a few hundred rapid verdicts in one sitting. The review-tool patterns from the 2026-07-25 waves exist; #745 (compare-and-contrast mode) and #929 (verdict provenance) are the tooling issues to lean on or extend.
3. **Then close the loop**: approved assets flow to the #951 integration lane; rejects get recorded so they are not regenerated blind.

## Not claimed

- Not claiming any specific batch is good or bad -- the point is nobody can claim that yet, because they have not been looked at.
- Not proposing new tooling beyond what #745/#929 already scope -- if the existing review flow suffices, just run it.

Related: #745 (compare-and-contrast review mode), #929 (verdict provenance), #850 (post-approval coherence/dedup pass -- runs AFTER this), #951 (integration lane), #1024 (poster batch), #934 (cycle-closeout script).

issues.title: art(sweep): events name physical things the office never shows -- install a security system, no cameras appear; sweep events for asset refs, then bulk-generate
issues.body:
From the recorded playtest of v0.13.2, 2026-08-01 09:52 (`art_generated/audiodump/2026-08-01_09-52-08.transcript.md`, local-only; frames `f106_559s.jpg`, `f119_623s.jpg`).

## Observation

**[10:21]** "I'm going to install a security system. Hey, if I install a security system then the lab should get some security cameras. So let's get some security cameras as art assets and let's do a sweep of all of our in-game events for reference to assets. And then use that to generate another 50 or 100 assets now."

Frames: the "Equipment Gone Missing" event offers `[Q] Install Security System ($35,000)`. Pip took it. The office floor -- which DOES visibly react to other state (cat adoption at [8:24] "I now have an actual cat", staff sprites, server rack, water cooler) -- shows nothing for it. $35,000 spent, zero visible consequence in the world the player watches all game.

The general defect: events and upgrades NAME physical things (security system, equipment, laptops, computing clusters) that the office sim never shows. Every such reference is a pre-scoped, high-confidence asset brief going unused -- and the office has already proven the payoff pattern with the cat.

## Ask (Pip's, near-verbatim)

1. **Sweep**: walk `godot/data/` (events, actions, upgrades JSON) and extract every noun that implies a visible object or office change. Output a table: source id -> implied asset -> exists? -> office hook.
2. **Generate**: use the table to drive a bulk generation batch -- Pip sized it at "another 50 or 100 assets now" [10:39]. Spend policy is active (free to $100AUD/day until 2026-08-15). Pipelines: in-repo gpt-image-1 tooling (`tools/assets`) for icons/props, pixellab for office-floor sprites.
3. **Wire the exemplar**: security system install -> camera sprites appear in the lab. One end-to-end case proves the sweep->generate->integrate loop before the batch lands (#951 is the integration lane pattern).

## Not claimed

- Not claiming every event needs an asset -- the sweep produces the candidate list; curation is the review loop's job.
- Not claiming mechanics change -- purely visual consequence wiring.

Related: #951 (integration/closeout lane pattern), #900 (art ramp round-2 gap-fill -- this sweep is its shopping list), #925 (office W3 pre-build), #913 (office juice -- same visible-consequence family), #934 (cycle-closeout script for when the batch finishes).
